meta.title: Wing Fighter Strategy Guide
meta.tagline: Build stronger PvP formations. Understand your opponents. Invest where it counts.
meta.author: ashpool

content.html: One of the most interesting things about Wing Fighter is that the player with more Battle Power (BP) does not always win. You can beat someone much stronger on paper, then lose to someone weaker. Often, the difference is not how much you have upgraded. It is how your build matches up against theirs.

That is what got me interested in figuring out how this game really works. Which stats counter each other? Why does one formation survive an attack that destroys another? When is a new drone or sentinel actually an improvement, and when are you just spending resources to raise BP? The more I have tested, compared notes, and dug into the mechanics, the more I have found that good decisions matter as much as raw power.

This is my working guide to those decisions, with PvP as the main focus. It covers how to size up an opponent, choose a formation, strengthen the parts of your build that matter, and get more from limited resources. There is also a dedicated PvE section, because boss damage is important for progression. Some recommendations are well established; others are things I am still testing, and I will call out the difference.

Your chips are the foundation of each formation. The attributes you prioritize determine the type of build you’re creating, whether that’s Burn / Crit Resistance, Dodge / Crit Resistance, or Crit / Hit. From there, choose your drones, sentinel, Mech Spirits, and equipment to support that strategy. You can save three different formations to prepare for different opponents and game modes. See Chips — Focus on the Stats That Matter for manufacturing and upgrade advice.

content.title: Part 1 — Pick the right formation for the fight

cells: Strengths and when to use it
My most-used PvP offense. Three developed Burn drones deal damage that Dodge cannot stop. Healing, Crit Resistance, and damage reduction help you survive while Burn builds.

My preferred Star Scramble defense, but useful for offense too against opponents with low Hit. Dodge avoids normal hits, Crit Resistance stops crits when high enough, and healing helps you outlast opponents.

Useful against high-Dodge opponents when your Hit Rate exceeds their Dodge. It can also counter Burn builds by dealing enough damage to win before their Burn stacks become overwhelming. That depends heavily on the opponent’s Crit Resistance, which is why many PvP Burn builds invest in it.
Your boss-damage build. Start with Burn chips to reach 100% Burn Enhancement. As you gain more Burn Enhancement from other sources, replace those chips with Crit Rate to increase your damage.
Combines offensive Crit with protection against opposing Crit. I used it extensively, but later switched to Crit / Hit to retain a strong Hit option after adopting Dodge / Crit Resistance.

Useful against Burn-heavy opponents. Burn Decrease reduces their damage; Dodge still helps against normal attacks. Giving up Crit Resistance makes it less suitable as my default defense against common Crit builds.

content.title: 1. Burn / Crit Resistance — My Main PvP Offense

content.html: Burn / Crit Resistance is my primary PvP offense, used for roughly 80% of my attacks. Its biggest advantage is that Burn damage cannot be dodged and grows stronger as the fight progresses. The challenge is surviving long enough for that damage to build. Crit Resistance helps protect against fast Crit attacks, while healing and damage reduction keep you in the fight.

cells: Three well-developed Burn drones. Two maxed Ninjas plus Sagittarius are a strong starting lineup. Ninjas are inexpensive to fully evolve, while Sagittarius’s Flaming increases the combined damage from all your Burn stacks.
Arcglow or Doomblast for healing. Doomblast also increases Healing Enhancement as the fight progresses. Glimshade is another option, healing when the target is burning.

Aqua Spirit and Star Envoy are my core choices. For the third slot, Berserk Dragon provides damage reduction, Ladybug provides emergency healing, and Lantern increases Healing Enhancement. In my testing, Berserk Dragon is currently winning more fights than the other two, but it’s worth testing all three.
Crit Resistance by default, with matchup-specific counters when needed.

content.html: Given how powerful Evil Eye is in PvE Burn builds, you might expect it to work just as well in PvP. The difference is how you invest in your chips.

In PvP, you want to concentrate on one offensive attribute to overcome your opponent’s resistance. For this build, that’s Burn Enhancement, with Crit Resistance for defense. Evil Eye converts only the Crit Rate above your opponent’s Crit Resistance into Burn Crit Rate. It works extremely well in PvE, where bosses have no Crit Resistance. But splitting your PvP chips between Burn and Crit makes it harder to overcome either resistance, leaving too little Crit Rate for Evil Eye to be effective.

I’m testing whether Burn / Crit Resistance deserves priority earlier in progression, including on my smaller account. The main trade-off is that newer players often need a dedicated PvE Burn formation. As you gain more Burn Enhancement without chips, you can move your PvE build toward Crit and eventually free a formation slot for PvP Burn. See PvE Burn progression.

content.title: 2. Dodge / Crit Resistance — Default PvP Defense

content.html: Dodge / Crit Resistance is my preferred Star Scramble defense. Dodge can avoid up to 80% of ordinary attacks, while Crit Resistance prevents critical hits when it exceeds your opponent's Crit Rate. Combined with strong healing, this gives you a better chance of surviving multiple attacks.

cells: Gridstar with Healing Enhancement is an affordable starting point. Arcglow provides stronger healing, and Doomblast is a longer-term SSR option. See Sentinels for passives and upgrade advice.
Aqua Spirit provides lasting damage reduction after triggering; Ladybug gives an emergency heal when HP first drops below 30%; Berserk Dragon reduces incoming damage from the beginning of the fight.

Apus would be my ideal choice for Dodge/Heal because it increases maximum HP and improves healing from Ladybug or Blood Bat. In practice, I use three Burn drones across formations to concentrate my upgrade resources.
Crit Resistance when you want to counter a Crit-focused opponent; choose Burn Decrease against Burn-heavy attackers.

For physical builds, Hardrock is worth testing for its additional HP, particularly in Dodge/Heal formations. However, I’ve found that using the full Conqueror setup wins more fights, likely because its additional damage outweighs Hardrock’s HP advantage.

content.html: If an attacker fails to eliminate you in Star Scramble, Cheat Death and Ladybug can trigger again in the next battle. This makes Dodge/Heal particularly effective for defending against successive attackers.

Why I use Burn drones instead of Apus: Apus's first three activations each add 5% of base HP to maximum and current HP, for a total of 15%. That also strengthens healing from Mech Spirits like Ladybug or Blood Bat. Developing separate drone lineups is expensive, so I use my three Burn drones across formations. Sagittarius still contributes Flaming, which increases the combined damage from all Burn stacks in longer fights.

content.title: 3. Crit / Hit — Counter Dodge or Burn

content.html: Crit / Hit gives you two ways to counter an opponent. Against high Dodge, Hit Rate helps your attacks connect, while Crit Rate increases the chance of critical damage. Against Burn builds, the advantage is speed: Crit can deliver heavy damage early, potentially winning before Burn stacks and damage bonuses build up. That depends on overcoming the opponent's Crit Resistance, which is why many PvP Burn formations invest heavily in it.

cells: SavagePlate provides fast direct damage. Stormquill reduces enemy Damage Boost and, as a G-rarity sentinel, is much cheaper to fully evolve. Rendclaw is another strong option, but as an SSR sentinel, it’s a longer-term investment.
Toad Lord can build Crit Damage from normal weapon crits and remove Burn stacks. Other useful swaps include Venom Scorpion, Flame Stinger, and Gloom Moon, depending on what the opponent brings.
Hit Rate when your opponent relies on Dodge and the extra Hit helps you reach or exceed their Dodge.

content.html: Toad Lord needs successful weapon crits. When your Crit Rate is sufficiently above enemy Crit Resistance, it can build Crit Damage and remove Burn stacks from you, making conventional Crit a useful answer to some Burn builds. Against high-Crit-Resistance opponents, Toad Lord and Venom Scorpion both lose much of their value. Do not pair Toad Lord with Evil Eye. Evil Eye converts away the normal weapon crits Toad Lord needs to trigger its ability.

content.title: 4. PvE Burn — Start with Burn chips, grow into Crit

content.html: PvE Burn/Crit is my primary approach to boss damage. The goal is to reach 100% Burn Enhancement, then build Crit Rate so Evil Eye can convert it into Burn Crit Rate.

Early on, you'll need Burn chips to reach the 100% cap. As you gain Burn Enhancement from Camp Tech, Mech Spirits, and sentinel passives, you can replace those chips with Crit Rate which increases your total damage.
For example, with 80% Burn Enhancement from other sources, you need only 20% from chips. Once those other bonuses reach 100%, all your chips can focus on Crit Rate.
This is where Evil Eye becomes especially powerful. It converts a portion of your Crit Rate into Burn Crit Rate, depending on its level. Against a boss with no Crit Resistance:

items.html: Level 1: 100% Crit Rate × 20% conversion = 20% Burn Crit Rate. You’d need 400% Crit Rate to reach the 80% cap.
Level 13: 100% Crit Rate × 56% conversion = 56% Burn Crit Rate. You’d need only 143% Crit Rate to reach the 80% cap.

content.html: Once you reach the Burn Enhancement and Burn Crit Rate caps, focus on increasing Crit Damage and Defense Break to boost your damage further.

cells: Burn Enhancement to reach the 100% cap, then Crit Rate as your non-chip Burn bonuses improve.

Equip three Burn drones. Two maxed Ninjas are inexpensive to develop, and their +10% drone Crit Rate helps a PvE Burn/Crit setup with Evil Eye. Sagittarius adds Flaming, increasing the combined damage from all your Burn stacks. Lich or Lyra may become useful as you develop them. See Burn Drones for progression advice.

Evil Eye converts Crit Rate into Burn Crit Rate, while Star Envoy increases Burn damage with three equipped Burn drones. For the third Mech Spirit, use Dragon Emperor or Crimson Shadow. Both increase PvE damage. I currently prefer Dragon Emperor, but Crimson Shadow can perform just as well or better. Compare their damage bonuses at your current skill levels.

I currently use SavagePlate with gold and blue Crit Damage passives. I am developing a Flashstrike with gold Crit Damage to see whether its damage-boost skill can outperform that SavagePlate. Compare actual boss results rather than assuming the newer sentinel wins.

content.html: For the complete Evil Eye conversion formula and stat caps, see the mechanics reference.

Eventually, you can use the same Crit chips for PvE and PvP, swapping drones and Mech Spirits for each fight. Remove Evil Eye when switching to conventional PvP Crit, especially if using Toad Lord. That frees your third formation for another PvP build.

content.title: When a matchup is worth attacking

content.html: Before attacking, compare the opponent's combat stats with your own. Pilot Defense and Defense Break can make a major difference even when your chip attributes look favorable. The table below shows which formations to consider and when to skip.

cells: Compare your Hit against their Dodge. Use Crit / Hit when it exceeds their Dodge. If not, a Burn formation bypasses their Dodge through Burn-drone skills; a Dodge mirror can also work with much better Dodge and stronger pilots, drones, and sentinel. If none is favorable, skip.

Compare your Crit Resistance with their Crit Rate. If close or higher, use Dodge / Crit Resistance. If not, consider a Crit mirror only with stronger offense and supporting components. Otherwise skip.

Burn Decrease is one defense. Another is a fast Crit attack if their Crit Resistance is low enough: Burn takes time to ramp, and Crit may win first. Toad Lord can also remove Burn stacks when your weapons crit. Do not choose that route against high Crit Resistance.
Try Heal Reduction from your sentinel or passives.
The entire formation saved for defense when the event begins; locked for the whole event.
You can change your entire attacking build before each attack.
Whatever you have equipped at the moment they attack, even if it is your PVE build.
Your formation locks when you spawn and choose it. After dying and respawning, you can choose or change the formation again. Proxy mode defaults to Formation 1.

content.html: Pilots are a good place to check when a matchup feels harder than it should. Their Defense Break and Defense affect the damage you deal and take. After that, look at the attribute you need most for the formation: Hit, Crit Resistance, healing, or the Burn bonuses your drones rely on.
Battle Power (BP) measures progression, but it does not reliably predict who wins. Pilots, chip matchups, healing, and damage bonuses can make a lower-BP player much stronger in PvP.

Stay lean for team events. Star Scramble matchmaking and Hyper Battlefield placement appear to consider legion BP, so increasing BP without a comparable improvement in fighting strength can make your next opponent harder. Legion Technology is a common source of wasted BP: Electric or Reflect Enhancement adds little if you do not use those attributes. Choose Top Tech and equipment upgrades for the fights you actually play, not just the BP they add.

Attack, HP, and better equipment can absolutely be worth the BP. The trade-off is especially clear with sentinels: leveling beyond 80 adds stats and BP, but does not improve the active skill. In Star Scramble, lower-BP players also contribute by clearing defensive items and reducing enemy fuel so stronger teammates can focus on one-hit kills.

Hyper Battlefield has five tiers, BF5 through BF1, and BF1 is a substantial jump from BF2. Legion BP and past results both appear to affect placement, but the exact formula is not published. Invest in combat effectiveness first, and let BP follow.

content.title: Pilots — The stats that keep you competitive

content.html: Your pilot roster contributes four combat stats: Physical Defense Break (PDB), Energy Defense Break (EDB), Physical Defense (PD), and Energy Defense (ED). Break helps your attacks against the matching defense; PD and ED help you withstand opponents using those damage types. They matter in both straightforward fights and mirror matchups where neither player has a decisive chip counter.

cells: Helps your physical-damage attacks overcome the opponent’s PD.
Develop this if you use physical gear.
Helps your energy-damage attacks overcome the opponent’s ED.
Develop this if you use energy gear.
Protects you against an opponent’s physical attacks and PDB.
Keep improving it, whatever gear you use.
Protects you against an opponent’s energy attacks and EDB.
Keep improving it, whatever gear you use.

items.html: Pilot gaps explain a lot of losses. If your PDB or EDB trails their matching Defense by a wide margin, your damage suffers. If your PD or ED trails their Defense Break, you take more damage. A clever chip setup can help, but it cannot always overcome a large disadvantage in these underlying stats.
Keep developing pilots alongside everything else. Well-built pilots make every formation more competitive. Even when equipment upgrades look exciting, do not let your pilot stats fall behind.

content.title: Equip the right pilot for each fight

content.html: Your equipped pilot should match both the type of damage you deal and the type of damage your opponent deals.
If you use physical equipment:

items.html: Freya (PDB / PD) — Against physical opponents.
Hestia (PDB / ED) — Against energy opponents.

content.html: If you use energy equipment:

items.html: Lancelot (EDB / PD) — Against physical opponents.
Clotho (EDB / ED) — Against energy opponents.

content.html: Why does switching matter? Every pilot you’ve unlocked contributes Defense, Defense Break, and passive bonuses, even when unequipped. But your equipped pilot contributes 4× its normal Defense and Defense Break. The multiplier does not apply to passive bonuses.
Here’s an example using awakened SR pilots. Assume all four combat stats start at 2,500, including the bonuses from your unequipped pilots.

For Freya, Hestia, and Lancelot, awakening gives +100 to each of their two stats. Equipping them multiplies that to +400, adding 300 above their unequipped contribution. Clotho has different awakened stats: +120 EDB and +80 ED, giving her an additional 360 EDB and 240 ED when equipped.

Example: You’re using physical equipment and facing an energy-based opponent. Switching from Freya to Hestia keeps your Physical Defense Break at 2,800 while increasing your Energy Defense from 2,500 to 2,800. You gain protection against their attacks without giving up offensive strength.
Switching pilots is free, so choose the right one before each fight. Your Star Scramble defensive pilot is locked once the event begins.

content.title: Pilot Evolution, Awakening, and Extra Shards

content.html: Your first priority is awakening two SR pilots for your main damage type, one providing Physical Defense and the other Energy Defense. This lets you switch pilots based on your opponent while keeping the Defense Break stat that supports your attacks.

items.html: Energy equipment: Awaken Lancelot (EDB / PD) and Clotho (EDB / ED).
Physical equipment: Awaken Freya (PDB / PD) and Hestia (PDB / ED).

content.html: How pilot upgrades work
The first two evolutions use Pilot Badges and are relatively inexpensive. Later evolutions require shards for that specific pilot, with increasing costs as you approach six stars.
Once a pilot reaches six stars, any additional shards for that pilot become extra shards that can be used to evolve or awaken other pilots of the same rarity.
How to spend your shards
Save your selectable SR shards for the pilots you plan to equip and awaken.

While collecting SR shards, continue developing your N and R pilots, especially those close to six stars. These upgrades improve your stats and make future drops of those pilots’ shards available for other upgrades.

Manage your N and R extra shards carefully. R shards can become a bottleneck when awakening your second SR pilot. Make sure you have enough N and R extra shards available when you’re ready to awaken, rather than using them on other upgrades.
Extra shards needed for awakening
These costs are in addition to Pilot Badges. Every SR pilot awakening requires 1,800 Pilot Badges, plus 1,500 N, 800 R, and 800 SR extra shards.
What comes after your first two SR awakenings?
Continue developing your N and R roster to six stars. Then evaluate additional SR or R awakenings based on the stats and passive bonuses they provide.
If you regularly use both physical and energy equipment, consider awakening all four SR pilots so you can switch between both damage and defense types.
SSR awakenings are a longer-term investment because their shards are difficult to acquire.

content.title: Train useful passives, not empty BP

content.html: Training Guides improve a pilot's passive ability, up to level 10. Each level provides the same increase in effectiveness, but costs progressively more Guides. The cost is identical across pilot rarities, making SR and SSR pilots with strong PvP abilities particularly good investments.

Focus on passives that help you win PvP fights. It's generally more efficient to develop several useful pilots before maxing out one. Training also increases BP, but it doesn't improve Defense or Defense Break, so be selective. Do not invest Training Guides in N and R pilots whose abilities only benefit PvE. They inflate your BP without improving your PvP performance.

content.title: Chips — Focus on the Stats That Matter

content.html: Chip manufacturing is a long-term investment. Set up Auto Mode to look for the attributes you want across all three formations, and run it daily. As your Chip Factory levels up, it produces better-quality chips, helping you strengthen each build over time.

content.title: Pick chips for the formation you actually use

content.html: For everyday chip manufacturing, I recommend Auto Mode with “Stop when chip rating increases.” It’s a huge time-saver and a good way to steadily improve your chips.

The trade-off is that overall chip rating doesn’t always reflect the attributes you care about. A lower-rated chip might have better Dodge and Crit Resistance than a higher-rated one, for example. But as your factory levels up and produces better-quality chips, that’s a relatively small sacrifice for a huge amount of time saved.

When you’re changing a formation or looking for specific attributes, consider lowering the minimum chip grade and reviewing more chips manually. This gives you a better chance of finding the attributes you need, even on lower-rated chips.

content.title: Use the Chip Factory without babysitting it

content.html: The Chip Factory produces random attributes, and Auto Mode can watch for chips suited to more than one formation. Start with three attribute targets; the interface can accommodate roughly three to six, but a narrower selection is easier to review. Use OR when either attribute is useful and AND only when both must appear on the same chip.

In Burn builds, your three drones supply much of the damage. A finished lower-rarity drone can be more useful than a barely developed SR, so compare what each drone contributes before committing resources.

content.title: How to develop your Burn drones

content.html: Start with Ninja. It is inexpensive to fully evolve and gives you a developed Burn drone sooner than an R or SR option. Build toward two maxed Ninjas and a strong third drone. Sagittarius adds Flaming, increasing the combined damage of your Burn stacks; Lich is a more accessible R option that buffs Burn damage across your drone lineup.

cells: Affordable Burn damage while you accumulate resources
Sagittarius, Lich, or another developed Burn drone
Choose useful skills and upgrades you can complete
Developed Sagittarius, Lyra, Fornax, or a strong R/SR mix
Replace a Ninja when the new drone actually improves your results

content.html: R drones are usually cheaper to develop than SR drones. Lich offers a team-wide Burn benefit; Cerberus and Scorpion Lion are more situational. SR drones can become stronger with enough investment, but compare boss and PvP results before replacing a completed drone.

Burn stacks have a six-stack limit. A Burn-drone skill can add a stack, but adding a seventh does not create a seventh active stack: it replaces the oldest one. This matters when judging abilities that add extra stacks. Also remember that Burn-drone normal attacks can still miss, even though their skills and existing Burn damage do not use the normal Hit/Dodge check. The mechanics reference covers drone critical hits.

A drone has five passive slots, and full evolution develops each passive to level 7. That is 35 passive-level upgrades in total and requires 48 copies of that drone, including the original. Later star tiers consume multiple duplicates, so do not estimate the cost as one copy per upgrade. You can use drones of different rarities together.
When recasting drone passives, prioritize gold or purple results that support your build. Recasts earn additional milestone credit during the Drone Event.

Transposition is a way to move good passive rolls to a better-developed drone. It costs 300 diamonds. Both drones must be the same rarity, have at least five stars, and have no unsaved recast results. The five passive types and colors switch places, but each drone keeps its own passive levels. For example, you can roll a great passive on a five-star donor, then transpose those passive types onto a much more evolved drone.
Lich: its level-4 skill gives +15% Burn Damage for all drones throughout the battle; the exact stacking relationship with other damage bonuses has not been independently verified.

Experimental Quick Reload deserves caution in Burn builds. The July mechanics research observed some situations where it increased the interval between Burn ticks from one second to as much as 1.5 seconds. That could reduce boss damage even if the passive sounds beneficial. Test it before committing to it.

A sentinel can keep you alive, deal damage, or counter an opponent’s healing. Which one you develop depends on your formation and the passives available to you. Gridstar is a useful example of how much a strong passive combination can matter.

cells: Arcglow for more sustain, or Doomblast as a longer-term SSR option
SavagePlate for repeated damage; Stormquill if you need to reduce enemy Damage Boost
Rendclaw when you need a stronger anti-heal answer
SavagePlate with gold + blue Crit Damage is my current working PvE sentinel; Flashstrike is a strong candidate I am developing.
Flashstrike with multiple Crit Damage passives and Sentinel Enhancement is a promising PvE goal, but compare boss damage before replacing a strong SavagePlate.
Arcglow for sustain or Glimshade if enemies stay burned

content.html: For Dodge / Heal defense, start with Gridstar and Healing Enhancement. Arcglow and Doomblast provide stronger healing options as you develop them, although rerolling multiple ideal passives on expensive sentinels can consume a lot of Protection Cores. Against heavy healing, keep a separate sentinel with Healing Reduction.

All five sentinel rarities (N, R, G, SR, and SSR) have four passive slots. Fully evolving one takes 40 total copies, including the first copy, and raises all four passives to level 10. Evolution also increases Attack and HP, but improving the passive bonuses is usually the biggest reason to pursue all 40 copies.

Sentinel level is separate from evolution. Overclock Chips raise the level and improve the active skill up to level 80. Levels 81–150 cost sharply more chips and raise raw stats and BP without making the skill stronger. Level 80 is a practical stopping point for many players, but pushing higher can make sense when raw strength is the goal. If you reset a sentinel, you can recover the Overclock Chips.

cells: Gold Healing Enhancement, then purple; Crit Damage Reduction or Sentinel Enhancement when useful.
Crit Damage, Crit Rate, Heal Reduction, and selected Sentinel Enhancement.
Crit Damage and useful damage buffs; Flashstrike can use a developed combination of multiple Crit Damage passives.
Healing Enhancement on Arcglow/Doomblast; Sentinel Enhancement if the sentinel’s own output matters.

content.html: At passive level 10, Healing Enhancement provides +100% for gold, +80% for purple, and +60% for blue. These bonuses add together. Gold Sentinel Enhancement adds +75% at level 10 and acts as a separate multiplier for eligible sentinel damage and healing. It does not multiply Ladybug or Cheat Death healing. Enemy Healing Reduction and Sentinel Reduction can offset the corresponding bonuses.

Not every heal uses the same bonuses. Apus increases maximum HP by 5% of base HP on each of its first three skill activations, up to +15% total. That increases percentage-of-Max-HP healing from Ladybug and Blood Bat. Cheat Death uses fundamental HP instead, while Doomblast and Arcglow heal based on Attack. Apus’s own HP recovery does not benefit from Healing Enhancement; Ladybug and Cheat Death do. The mechanics research also indicates that Glimshade’s conditional heal benefits from Healing Enhancement but not the Sentinel Enhancement multiplier.

content.title: The real cost of a sentinel recast

content.html: Every sentinel recast costs 20 Recast Cores, regardless of the number of locked passive slots. Locking slots protects good rolls, but each lock adds a separate Protection Core cost on every attempt:

Protection Cores are particularly expensive. At the first-pack rate of 15 for $3 (where available), locking one slot uses about $4 of Protection Cores per recast; two cost about $8; three about $20. Those amounts are in addition to the 20 Recast Cores. Later paid packs can be more expensive. Save the costly recasts for the sentinels where a better passive will make the most difference. The reference section models the odds of finding a specific gold passive.

content.title: Keep the better passive, not the older sentinel

content.html: Gridstar shows why passive quality matters. Each inexpensive new copy starts with one passive, so you can look for a gold Healing Enhancement roll and then transfer your existing evolution progress through reverse merging.

Reverse merging lets you keep a great passive on a newer copy. Select the sentinel you keep, which has the passive you want, and the developed sentinel you sacrifice. The kept sentinel retains its existing passive rolls and receives the evolution stars. New passive slots gain new random rolls. All passive rolls on the sacrificed sentinel disappear.

For example, suppose you have an old 40-star Arcglow with mediocre passives and find a one-star Arcglow with gold Healing Enhancement. Keep the one-star copy and sacrifice the 40-star copy into it. You keep the gold passive and end up with a developed Arcglow. Level down the old sentinel before sacrificing it so you recover the Overclock Chips.

cells: 1,450% Attack every 4s; heals 30% of damage if enemy burning (PVP only)
Heals 360% Attack every 4s (PVP); +15% Final Damage Decrease for 2s
Heals 480% Attack every 4s (PVP); +10% Healing Enhancement each activation, up to +50%

content.html: Doomblast’s Healing Enhancement stacks build over time: each 10% stack begins after the heal that triggered it, so the next heal benefits. Flashstrike’s two-second Damage Boost can be helpful for damage dealt during that window, but the exact interaction with newly applied Burn stacks has not been independently tested.

You can equip three Mech Spirits. Pick them for the formation you are using: healing and damage reduction for a long defensive fight, weapon-crit bonuses for Crit offense, or Burn-specific bonuses for PvE. Mech Spirit combinations and passive bonuses also improve your account even when the spirit is not equipped.

items.html: Aqua Spirit (SSR): Its Emergency Shield grants +35% Final Damage Decrease the first time your HP crosses its threshold. At skill level 1 that threshold is below 30% HP; at level 13 it rises to below 96%. The protection lasts until the battle ends, even after you heal. That makes it especially valuable in healing builds.
Berserk Dragon (SR): Grants Final Damage Decrease from the start of the fight until the end: +10% at skill level 1, reaching +34% at level 13. Unlike Aqua Spirit, it has no low-HP trigger.

Lantern: Increases Healing Enhancement starting four seconds into the battle, from +17% at skill level 1 to +53% at level 13. It is worth testing as a third Mech Spirit when healing helps you survive long PvP fights.

Ladybug (N): Provides a one-time emergency heal when your HP first falls below 30% in a PvP battle. It restores 6.25% of maximum HP at skill level 1, growing to 21.25% at level 13. Healing Enhancement improves the result. Ladybug cannot be chosen with selectable Mech rewards, so Mech Event pulls are the main way to develop it.

content.html: Aqua Spirit’s protection stays active after the HP threshold is crossed, even if you heal afterward. Ladybug supplies a separate one-time emergency heal when HP first falls below 30%. For PvP Burn, damage reduction can be more valuable than another heal: in my testing, Berserk Dragon currently wins more fights in the third slot than Ladybug or Lantern, though matchups and Mech Spirit levels matter.

Aqua Spirit and Berserk Dragon contribute to the same Final Damage Decrease stat. Their listed +35% and +34% bonuses are valuable together, but do not interpret them as a literal 69% reduction in every incoming hit: the combat formula also depends on the attacker’s other damage modifiers.

items.html: Toad Lord (SR): Conventional weapon crits can trigger its effect every two seconds. Each trigger removes three Burn stacks from you and increases Crit Damage until the battle ends, up to eight stacks. At skill level 1, eight stacks total +60% Crit Damage; at level 13 they total +204%. It is less reliable against opponents with strong Crit Resistance. Do not pair it with Evil Eye, which removes the normal weapon crits Toad Lord needs. Against Burn builds stacked with Crit Resistance, it may barely trigger, so do not assume it will reliably clear their Burn.
Venom Scorpion: Useful with conventional Crit offense when the opponent’s Crit Resistance does not prevent most of your crits. Against high resistance, expect less value.
Flame Stinger: A damage-finishing option when the opponent is low on HP. Gloom Moon is a Hit Rate counter for high Dodge; Battle Diva helps against heavy Crit.

Evil Eye (SR): Converts Crit Rate remaining after the target’s Crit Resistance into Burn Crit Rate. At skill level 1, every 10% eligible Crit Rate produces about 2% Burn Crit Rate; at level 13, it produces 5.6% and adds +25.5% Burn Damage Boost. It is a cornerstone of this PvE strategy, not a replacement for normal weapon Crit in PvP.

Star Envoy (SSR): Requires three equipped Burn drones. Every third Burn-drone skill has a chance to add a stack of Burn Damage Boost, up to five stacks. The activation chance increases as your Burn Enhancement exceeds the enemy’s Burn Decrease. The maximum stacked bonus is +125% at skill level 1 or +425% at level 13. Star Envoy is a powerful long-term upgrade for Burn builds.

Third Mech Spirit: Use Dragon Emperor or Crimson Shadow. Both increase PvE damage. I currently prefer Dragon Emperor, but testing has shown that Crimson Shadow can perform just as well or better. Compare their damage bonuses at your current skill levels to see which performs best.

content.html: Mech Spirits improve their attribute bonuses during each four-level stretch. Every fifth level upgrades their main skill. The skill reaches level 13 when the spirit reaches level 60. You also get some benefits from spirits that are not equipped, so plan upgrades around the active skills and collection bonuses you can actually use.

cells: You are attacking a high-Dodge opponent.
You are defending against Crit-heavy opponents; useful default for Star Scramble defense.
The opponent relies on that specific damage type.

content.html: You equip one engine, but some engine grades also offer shared bonuses. Compare the equipped and shared values when choosing which to develop.

Camp and Super Technology offer broadly useful PvP bonuses, including Final Damage Increase, Final Damage Decrease, PvP Damage, and PvP Damage Reduction. For PvE Burn, additional Burn Enhancement can free chips for Crit Rate. Compare the next available upgrade cost with the benefit to your current build.

content.title: Prioritize upgrades that help your formations

content.html: Start with broadly useful PvP damage and protection bonuses, then improve attributes that address your current matchups. Check the cost of the next level before investing.

items.html: Final Damage Increase (FDI) and Final Damage Decrease (FDD): useful broad PvP improvements. FDI helps your outgoing damage; FDD helps reduce incoming damage. Prioritize whichever is affordable and addresses your current losses. The exact formula belongs in the mechanics reference, not in your first upgrade decision.
PvP Damage and PvP Damage Reduction: another set of broadly useful PvP bonuses. Compare the cost of the next level with FDI/FDD rather than assuming you must max one track first.
Burn Enhancement: especially valuable to a PvE Burn build until you can keep 100% effective Burn Enhancement without using Burn chips.

Hit Rate, Crit Resistance, Dodge, and Crit Rate: buy the stats that solve an actual problem in your matchups. Level 10 can be a convenient place to reassess costs, but it is not a required stopping point.

content.html: Basic Camp Technology upgrades Maingun, Winggun, Missile Attack, and HP across different camps. Some early levels may be quite cheap. Compare the price of each upgrade with the benefit to your fighter.

In Camp → Super Technology, SkyEagle Tech increases Final Damage Increase. Crystal Prism, Eternal Pivot, and later Source Essence provide Final Damage Decrease. These are useful across several PvP formations. Compare the next upgrade cost and effect rather than chasing one fixed level target.

Titan gear affects your damage type and the Defense Break stat you need from pilots. A complete matching set can also improve the attack value used by weapons and other damage sources, so compare the full set before swapping a single piece.

items.html: Conqueror (physical): Use matching Conqueror Titan equipment with your Conqueror fighter to get the applicable set bonuses. The fighter and gear-set requirements are different things.
Destroyer (energy): A popular energy-damage direction. Titan Challenge seasons can favor different equipment, so compare your damage in the current season before spending scarce shards.
Thor (energy): Another energy set. It may be worth developing certain pieces for a Titan season, but evaluate them against the Destroyer pieces you already have.

content.html: The July mechanics model gives a 1.3× adjusted-attack factor for a complete five-piece Titan setup. Because several damage sources use adjusted attack, replacing one piece can cost more than its individual stats suggest. My full Conqueror setup has also won more fights than switching to Hardrock for extra HP. Compare complete builds in actual fights, including their set bonuses.
Before using gear as upgrade material, check whether it is part of a matching Titan set and what you would lose by removing it. Two pieces with similar BP may still produce very different damage.
Prism Winggun is a useful temporary PvE option until you obtain Destroyer Winggun. Its value depends on your current equipment and upgrades.

content.title: Legion Technology — Prioritize aerial PVP bonuses

content.html: Focus Legion Technology on upgrades that help your actual formations. The aerial-enemy damage and damage-reduction bonuses explicitly include other players, making them valuable across PvP builds. Unused Electric or Reflect attributes can add BP without helping you fight.

For PvP, pay attention to two upgrades that explicitly include other players: “Increase damage against aerial enemies (including players)” in Damage Increase, and “Reduce damage from aerial enemies (including players)” in Enemy Weakened. Their listed maximum level is 100. These can help across a wide range of PvP attacks and defenses, so they deserve sustained investment.

Equipment Reinforce lets you improve individual weapons through Base Attack, Attack Rate, Crit Rate, and Crit Damage. Prioritize the weapons that contribute the most damage to your current formation, accounting for upgrade costs:

items.html: Compare your weapons. Maingun, Winggun, and Missile contribute differently in Conqueror and Destroyer builds. Upgrade the one with the strongest payoff for its next cost.

Choose the stat for the situation. Base Attack raises direct output. Crit Rate matters when your attacks can still gain from more crits, including against PvP Crit Resistance. Crit Damage helps most when you already land crits reliably.
Do not dismiss Attack Rate. More attacks can compete with bigger hits. Compare current cooldowns, damage, and upgrade prices; a single fixed order cannot capture every build.

content.html: For example, the mechanics model lists a rainbow Titan Winggun at roughly 1.6 seconds between shots with a damage coefficient of 0.09, and Missile at about four seconds with a coefficient of 0.225. Those numbers partly offset one another before considering weapon attack values, crits, and other bonuses. Compare the actual contribution and upgrade cost of each weapon when choosing what to improve next.

If you are dying before you can do meaningful damage, Armor HP may be more useful than another weapon upgrade. For PvP, prioritize the aerial-enemy bonuses that apply to other players over bonuses meant mainly for bosses or ground targets.

Event milestones change the value of when you spend. If you are close to completing a reward round, saving tickets or currency for the next event may be better than spending a little now and losing that progress when the event resets.

content.title: Know the milestone before you spend

content.html: Check the reward milestones before spending. Several events allow four rounds, but the best stopping point differs: the Mech Event, for example, can make 100 or 500 pulls more attractive than stopping at 400.

cells: 100 pulls is an efficient partial target; 500 (400+100) can be better than stopping at 400, if affordable
Save enough for a full 300-pull round; diamond pulls can help reach another round
Bank for a complete round; purchase milestones reset each event
8,000 Rhenite eligible spend; up to 4 rounds
Use buy/sell refunds and event-credit drone recasts
No verified universal target in this guide

content.html: The Mech Event has 400 pulls per full reward round. Because the rewards in the first 100 pulls can be especially attractive, two practical stopping points are 100 pulls when resources are limited, or 500 pulls if you can afford to finish a 400-pull round and claim the first 100 pulls of the second. Do not assume 400 is always the best place to stop. Check the current reward screen before spending, as the exact rewards have not been independently verified for every event. Ladybug has no N-class selectable, so random Mech Event pulls are particularly important for developing it.
Choose your stopping point based on the current rewards and how close you are to the next round.

content.title: Drone Event — How resale changes the cost

content.html: A full Drone Event round takes 8,000 Rhenite in qualifying spend, with up to four rounds. Buying a drone counts at full price, but selling it returns 80% of what you paid. If all 8,000 is spent on drones and resold, the net cost is 1,600 Rhenite. Progress resets between events.

Refreshes cost 10 Rhenite and count toward the milestone, but cannot be refunded. For example, 26 refreshes cost 260, plus 7,800 in drone purchases, for 8,060 event credit. Selling the drones returns 6,240, so the net cost is 1,820 Rhenite. Drone recasts also count toward the event; budget for them separately.

Save your drone recasts for Drone Events when possible. Modified Chips count at twice their value toward event milestones, so you can improve drone passives while earning event rewards. Your net Rhenite cost depends on purchases, refunds, refreshes, and recasts. The Drone Event Calculator can help plan a round. With a Volley Vortex pass, completing four rounds may be easier; some active players can complete two or three without one.

A full Pilot Event reward round takes 300 pulls, and up to four rounds may be completed in one event. Milestone progress resets between events. Save Recruitment Tickets until you can reach a full round rather than buying scattered partial rewards. Active players may manage one round, and sometimes two with diamonds. SR pilot selectables are especially useful for developing the pilots you plan to equip and awaken.

A full Sentinel Event reward round requires 8,000 Sentinel Chips spent. Progress resets at the next event, and up to four rounds (32,000 total spend) can be completed in one event. If you cannot reach 8,000, saving for the next event is often better than spending partway toward a milestone you will lose. Finishing a round awards a selectable SSR sentinel in addition to anything purchased from the shop.

The shop offers four free refreshes a day. Paid refreshes cost 10 Sentinel Chips each. Free and paid refreshes advance the SSR refresh counters, which carry over between events. One SSR is guaranteed after every 20 refreshes in that counter. A random bonus SSR can appear earlier without resetting the 20-refresh count.

There is also a separate preferred-SSR counter. Choose the SSR you want. After five nonpreferred SSR appearances, the next refresh guarantees your preferred SSR; you do not have to buy those five to advance the counter. Changing your preferred selection does not reset it. When the preferred SSR appears, the counter resets even if you do not buy that copy.

One useful tactic is to use the free refreshes before the event until your preferred SSR appears in the shop. Then stop refreshing. When the event starts, purchase that SSR so its 1,000-chip price counts toward the new 8,000-chip milestone. You can buy only one copy per SSR appearance. Depending on refreshes and luck, a full event round may produce roughly four or five preferred copies through the shop, plus the selectable SSR reward. Lower-rarity purchases can help finish the spending milestone, but watch your inventory space. Extra slots have cost 500 diamonds.

Fully evolving an SSR sentinel requires 40 total copies, so treat it as a long-term investment. Collecting the right sentinels for a combination can also provide a bonus. Activate that bonus manually once you have the required sentinels; its behavior after selling one of them has not been verified.

content.title: Daily diamonds — Spend on your current bottleneck

content.html: Decide which upgrade you are working toward before spending daily diamonds. Pilot awakening, drone evolution, sentinel passives, and event milestones draw on different resources; focus your spending on the next meaningful upgrade and keep enough diamonds in reserve for upcoming events.

An aggressive daily routine can cost about 540 diamonds: 140 for engine parts, 300 across three challenge resources, and 100 for Chip Factory parts. Spend based on your current bottleneck rather than treating this as a daily requirement.
The reference below covers the numbers behind the recommendations: Defense Break, stat caps, Burn Crit conversion, drone effects, and recast odds.

content.title: Defense Break vs. Defense — Exact math

content.html: Defense Break is an offensive stat; Defense is the matching defensive stat. For physical damage, compare your PDB against the target’s PD. For energy damage, compare your EDB against the target’s ED. The difference between those values changes your outgoing damage. Reverse the comparison to understand incoming damage: their PDB versus your PD, or their EDB versus your ED.
If your Break ≥ enemy Defense (neutral or bonus zone):
Damage Multiplier = 1 + ((Your Break − Enemy Defense) / 1000)
If your Break < enemy Defense (penalty zone):
Damage Multiplier = 1 / (1 + ((Enemy Defense − Your Break) / 1000))

You only need the gap between Break and Defense to apply the formula. At equal values, the multiplier is 1.00×. A positive gap increases damage; a negative gap reduces it. For example, if your PDB is 300 above their PD, the bonus-side formula gives 1.30× before other modifiers. The reverse comparison tells you how well your defenses hold up against the opponent.

When your Break equals their Defense, damage is at the neutral 1.00× multiplier. The effect changes smoothly as the gap changes: parity is a convenient comparison point, not a sudden cliff. Increasing Defense Break above parity can still help, so do not stop just because the two numbers match.

Below parity, a given negative gap reduces damage by less than the same positive gap increases it. That is because the penalty uses a reciprocal formula. The table shows both directions so you can see the size of the difference:

cells: Closing a deficit improves every hit.
At −500, damage is about two-thirds of normal.

content.html: When your Break is far below the opponent’s Defense, closing that gap can be a very valuable upgrade. But the formula has no magic threshold: compare the cost of more Break with your other available improvements.

content.title: Stat caps and which attacks use them

content.html: Most of these are effective caps after accounting for the opponent’s defenses. A displayed stat above a cap may still help in PvP because the opponent cancels some of it. For example, 150% displayed Crit Rate against 70% Crit Resistance leaves 80% effective Crit Rate.

cells: Effective after opponent Burn Decrease. PVE bosses have none; PVP may require more than 100% raw to reach the cap.
Your dodge minus opponent's hit rate; raw dodge can exceed 80%.
Your crit rate minus opponent's crit resistance; raw crit can exceed 80%.
80% effective for ordinary direct crits and for Burn Crit Rate; displayed Crit Rate may exceed 80%, which matters for Evil Eye conversion.

content.html: Different attacks follow different rules. Normal weapon hits and drone normal attacks can miss against Dodge. Drone skills, sentinel skills, and Mech Spirit skills generally do not use that same Hit Rate roll. This is why a Burn-drone skill can still damage a high-Dodge opponent even if ordinary attacks miss.

items.html: Normal weapon and drone attacks: Hit Rate and Dodge matter. Weapon crit chance uses global and weapon-specific stats; drone normal attacks normally need Spot Weakness to crit.
Drone, sentinel, and Mech Spirit skills: generally hit without the normal Hit Rate check, and normally do not crit.
With Evil Eye: Burn-drone normal attacks and skills gain a special way to crit using converted Crit Rate.

content.html: This distinction explains why a sentinel that deals damage through a skill does not need Hit Rate in the same way your normal weapon attacks do. It also explains why improving Dodge cannot stop a Burn skill that has already applied its damage-over-time effect.

content.title: How much Burn Enhancement is useful?

content.label: Hard cap
content.html: The burning-drone enhancement multiplier is capped at 2.0× (a maximum +100% effective enhancement), and floored at 1.0×. In the combat-mechanics model, the net bonus depends on your Burning Enhancement minus the enemy’s Burning Decrease. That means how much raw enhancement you need depends on the actual target:

A quick example: against an opponent with 50% Burn Decrease, 100% raw Burn Enhancement leaves you with only 50% effective enhancement. Reaching the full 100% effective bonus would require 150% raw. This is why “100% Burn” is a natural PvE target but not always enough for PvP.

items.html: PVE against a boss with no Burning Decrease: 100% raw Burning Enhancement reaches the 100% effective bonus cap. Beyond that, more enhancement adds nothing against that target. Do not assume every PVE enemy has identical defenses without checking.
PVP vs. opponent with no Burn Decrease: Same as PVE, 100% raw = 100% effective. Past 100% does nothing.
PVP vs. opponent with 50% Burn Decrease: Need 150% raw burn to deliver 100% effective. Burn chips past 150% start to over-shoot.
PVP vs. opponent with 100% Burn Decrease: Need 200% raw burn to deliver 100% effective. Still capped at 100% effective, just takes more raw to get there.

content.html: In this multiplier, effective Burn Enhancement is your raw Burn Enhancement minus the target’s Burn Decrease, with a floor of 0% and a cap of 100%. The multiplier therefore ranges from 1× to 2×.
For the chip-swapping strategy, see PvE Burn / Crit.

There are two separate numbers to keep in mind: displayed Crit Rate and effective critical-hit chance. Regular critical hits cannot exceed an 80% effective chance after subtracting the target’s Crit Resistance. Your displayed Crit Rate, however, can rise much higher. Evil Eye uses the eligible displayed Crit Rate, including the amount above 80%, to create Burn Crit Rate. Burn Crit Rate has its own 80% effective cap.

Evil Eye (SR Mech Spirit) converts Crit Rate left after the target’s Crit Resistance. At skill level 1, 10% eligible Crit Rate converts to about 2% Burn Crit Rate. At level 13 (Mech Spirit level 60), 10% converts to 5.6%, and Evil Eye also grants +25.5% Burn Damage Boost at battle start. If the PvE target has no Crit Resistance, approximately 142.9% displayed Crit Rate reaches the 80% Burn Crit Rate cap at maximum Evil Eye. Players generally observe little or no PvE Crit Resistance, but that assumption has not been independently verified for every enemy.

cells: Max Evil Eye Burn Crit Rate

content.html: Evil Eye converts the eligible Crit Rate left after enemy Crit Resistance, so PvP requires more raw Crit Rate to obtain the same Burn Crit Rate. Do not pair Evil Eye with Toad Lord: Toad Lord needs normal weapon crits, which Evil Eye converts away.

Without Evil Eye, drone normal attacks do not use your ordinary global Crit Rate. They need the Spot Weakness passive to crit. Raging Assault increases the damage of those drone crits, so it is most useful when you already have a way to land them. Spot Weakness can work on its own; Raging Assault does little for a drone that cannot crit.

items.html: With Evil Eye: Burn-drone normal attacks and skills can crit using Evil Eye’s converted Crit Rate and the global Crit Damage multiplier. That replaces their normal Spot Weakness/Raging Assault crit calculation for these attacks.
Burn ticks: The separate damage-over-time ticks do not themselves crit. Burn Crit Rate refers to the eligible Burn-drone attacks, not every individual damage-over-time tick.

content.html: My current preference is Lich among accessible R Burn drones, because its skill helps Burn damage across your whole drone trio. Cerberus and Scorpion Lion depend more on specific conditions. The July mechanics research did not prove an exact damage ranking, and Lich’s interaction with Sagittarius or Star Envoy is still uncertain.

cells: Listed +15% burn-damage bonus; exact stacking with other burn buffs unverified
A broadly useful team bonus, but do not count it as an independent 1.15× multiplier on every Burn tick. It may share the same bonus pool as other Burn buffs.
255% skill coefficient and +3.5% listed bonus per Burn stack; exact interaction unverified
The bonus depends on current Burn stacks. Mechanics research suspects it multiplies the skill’s damage rather than simply adding to its listed coefficient, but the exact interaction needs testing.
+1 burn stack when recoil is active
More Burn stacks can help under the six-stack limit, but a new stack replaces the oldest when the target is already full. The recoil condition also has to be met.

content.html: Cerberus and Scorpion Lion have different conditional effects, and there isn’t enough controlled comparison data to rank every R Burn drone conclusively.

content.title: Sentinel recast odds and duplicate rules

content.html: Each developed sentinel can have up to four passive slots. The rates below describe what a given available slot might roll, not your chance of getting a perfect full set. Some passive combinations are restricted, so the exact odds after you lock several slots are not fully documented.
Gold rolls are uncommon but not impossibly rare. A specific gold passive, such as Gold Healing Enhancement, is much harder to find.

content.title: Cost of hunting a specific gold passive

content.html: This is a planning estimate, not a promise about the game’s actual random-number behavior. It assumes that every unlocked passive slot has an independent 0.5% chance to roll the one specific gold passive you want. Locking a good existing roll protects it but leaves fewer open slots for the next attempt.

The dollar estimates assume 20 Recast Cores per attempt at $3 for 20. They exclude the separate cost of Protection Cores, which can become much larger once you lock slots. They also ignore free materials. Duplicate-passive rules could affect the real probability.

Different colors of the same passive can coexist: for example, Gold Healing Enhancement and Purple Healing Enhancement can occupy separate sentinel slots. You cannot rely on getting two copies of the same type and color. The exact handling when some rolls are unavailable is not fully documented, so treat the probabilities as estimates.

A sentinel with one great gold passive and several useful supporting passives is already a success. The odds of landing a second exact gold can be expensive, and those same materials might make your drones, pilots, or another sentinel stronger. Chase a second ideal gold when the rest of your build is ready for that investment.
